title: Why is PolicyEngine higher than Census SPM?
summary: PolicyEngine's 2024 SPM-like rate is much higher than Census's 2024 SPM rate.
Adding child support received and workers' compensation to PE SPM resources closes only a small share of the gap.
Raw CPS ASEC with Census-reported SPM resources can closely replicate the Census report, so PolicyEngine's SPM threshold formula is not the main driver.

The Table B-5 threshold-ratio distribution shows PE has much more mass below the poverty line than Census, pointing toward the enhanced CPS income distribution, reweighting, universe, and threshold pipeline.
Census SPM resource aggregates are validation controls, not inputs for ECPS construction or clone imputation.

admin_calibration_targets.source: OCSS FY 2024 Preliminary Data Report and Tables
admin_calibration_targets.target: Use one gross-flow target for received and paid child support, then keep net child support as received minus paid.
admin_calibration_targets.implementation_note: OCSS administrative totals are the best timely state-level source, but they mostly cover child-support-program collections and state disbursement-unit flows, not all private informal payments.

admin_calibration_targets.source: Census SPM technical documentation and HHS LIHEAP FY2024 profile
admin_calibration_targets.target: Target LIHEAP-style energy assistance by state, including heating, cooling, crisis, and weatherization/home-repair components where the benefit is part of SPM resources.
admin_calibration_targets.implementation_note: Census says energy assistance includes LIHEAP or similar state/local programs, not LIHEAP alone.

admin_calibration_targets.source: Census Table B-6 footnote, Census SPM tech doc, USAC ACP data
admin_calibration_targets.target: Use energy assistance plus ACP/EBB internet assistance. ACP should be part-year in 2024 because the federal program ended in June.
admin_calibration_targets.implementation_note: Current PE 2024 data has ACP/EBB at zero, so utility assistance equals energy assistance until broadband benefits are populated.

admin_calibration_targets.source: NASI 2022 state summaries, uprated with NCCI indemnity severity
admin_calibration_targets.target: Use NASI cash benefits by state: total benefits times one minus medical-benefit share.
admin_calibration_targets.implementation_note: A reasonable first 2022-to-2024 uprating factor is 1.05 * 1.06 = 1.113, using NCCI rounded indemnity severity growth for 2023 and 2024. Use state-specific NCCI severity if we need more precision.
